app.name: Freelief
app.tagline: Breathe with the circle. You are safe right now.
nav.label: Screens
nav.breatheHint: Follow the circle in and out.
nav.groundHint: Notice what is around you, one sense at a time.
nav.bubblesHint: Slow, soft bubbles. Pop as many as you like.
nav.traceHint: Follow a slow loop with your finger or the arrow keys.
nav.sortHint: Put soft colours in order, from light to dark.
nav.settingsHint: Breathing rhythm, soft tones and colours.
breathe.title: Breathe
breathe.paused: Paused. Resume when you are ready.
ground.title: Ground yourself
ground.intro: Take your time. There is no right answer.
ground.5: Look around you. Find five things you can see.
ground.4: Notice four things you can touch or feel. Your feet on the floor. Your hands.
ground.3: Listen. Find three things you can hear.
ground.2: Notice two things you can smell, or two smells you like.
ground.1: Notice one thing you can taste, or take one slow sip of water.
ground.done: Well done. You are here, in this moment.
statements.title: Calming words
statements.list: This feeling is strong, and it will pass.
You have felt this before, and it passed.
Your body is trying to protect you. You are safe right now.
You do not have to fight it. Let it rise, and let it fall.
Breathe out slowly. Your heart can slow down too.
These feelings are uncomfortable, but they will fade.
Feel your feet on the ground. You are here.
It is okay to feel this way.
You are doing well. Stay with it.
bubbles.title: Pop bubbles
bubbles.intro: Tap a bubble, or move to one and press Enter. There is nothing to win.
trace.title: Trace a shape
trace.intro: Move the dot slowly around the loop with your finger, or with the arrow keys. Go at your own pace.
trace.oneLoop: One loop. Keep going for as long as you like.
trace.loops: {count} loops. Keep going for as long as you like.
sort.title: Sort colours
sort.intro: Put the tiles in order, from lightest on the left to darkest on the right. Choose a tile, then choose the tile to swap it with. Arrow keys move between tiles.
sort.chosen: {name} chosen. Now choose the tile to swap it with.
sort.done: All in order, from lightest to darkest. Choose New colours for another set, or stay here.
settings.title: Settings
settings.tonesHint: Gentle sounds that mark breathing in and out. Off unless you turn them on.

footer.label: About Freelief
about.title: About Freelief
about.selfHelp1: Freelief is a free self-help tool for moments of panic or strong anxiety. It is not medical care. It does not diagnose or treat any condition, and it does not replace a doctor, a therapist or emergency services.
about.selfHelp2: If panic attacks happen often, or change how you live, please talk to a doctor or a mental health professional. Effective help exists.
about.selfHelp3: If you are in danger, or might harm yourself, use "Need urgent help?" at the top of every screen, or call your local emergency number.
about.privacy1: Freelief collects nothing about you. It has no account, no analytics and no advertising, and it sends nothing over the internet after it is installed.
about.privacy2: Your settings (breathing rhythm, tones and colours) are saved only on this device. Clearing your browser data removes them.
about.open1: Freelief is free to use and its source code is open, under the MIT license.
standards.title: Standards and research
standards.verifiedIntro: Freelief meets these standards. Each one was checked by people, with a screen reader and with a keyboard only, for this version:
standards.none: Freelief is built to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, and level AAA where it can. Automated accessibility checks run on every screen of every version. We do not claim a standard yet: a standard is shown here only after people check Freelief with a screen reader and with a keyboard only.
standards.help: You can help: check Freelief with your screen reader or keyboard and tell us what you find.
standards.researchIntro: Every exercise in Freelief is built on a technique that has been studied in published research. No study has tested Freelief itself. Here is what each technique rests on, and how strong that evidence is.
standards.evidence.breathing: Slow breathing, especially with a longer breath out, has been studied in randomized trials and reviews. It was linked with better mood and calmer body signals, mostly in healthy adults. A trial in people with panic disorder used a breathing method with a monitor that Freelief does not have.
standards.evidence.grounding: The evidence is limited. One small study, with no comparison group, found less test anxiety after students learned this technique. Grounding is widely used, but it has not been tested in a randomized trial.
standards.evidence.statements: Steady, rehearsed coping statements are part of stress inoculation training, which reduced anxiety across many studies. They also follow the cognitive model of panic, in which panic grows from frightening thoughts about body sensations.
standards.evidence.distraction: Turning attention to a simple, structured task can ease strong feelings for a short time. But research also suggests that relying on distraction can keep anxiety going over the long term. Use these activities for the moment, and talk to a professional if panic comes back often.
feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.intro: Tell us what works, what does not, and how Freelief works with your screen reader or keyboard. Nothing is sent by Freelief itself: you read and edit the message, then send it yourself.
